title: NY State Assembly · District 46
area: Brooklyn: Brighton Beach, Coney Island, Bay Ridge, Sea Gate, and Dyker Heights

context.text: Chris McCreight (D) defeated Joseph Santangelo 64.2%–35.5% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary; a third Democrat, Marie Mirville-Shahzada, withdrew before the primary. McCreight also advanced from the Working Families Party primary without appearing on the ballot and holds the locally created Affordable & Safe Party line. Incumbent Alec Brook-Krasny (R, C) advanced from the Republican and Conservative Party primaries, both canceled, without appearing on the ballot. McCreight previously lost to Brook-Krasny in the 2024 general election.

candidates.name: Alec Brook-Krasny
candidates.currentRole: Member, NY State Assembly (since January 2023; previously 2007-2013)

summary.text: Alec Brook-Krasny is the Republican and Conservative Party incumbent in Assembly District 46, representing Brighton Beach, Coney Island, Bay Ridge, Sea Gate, and Dyker Heights. He returned to the Assembly in 2023 after previously serving from 2007 to 2013, and is seeking re-election.

background.text: Born in Moscow; his parents worked as a shoemaker and a bookkeeper. He earned dual degrees in Engineering and Economics from the Moscow Technological Institute.
Emigrated to Brooklyn speaking limited English and worked as a stockperson, then manager, at a Manhattan shoe store.
Founded Fun-O-Rama, a children's entertainment and community center in Coney Island, and was named 'Entrepreneur of the Year' by Leisure and Entertainment magazine in 1997.
Served on NYC Community Board 13, later as its treasurer, and founded the Council of Jewish Émigré Community Organizations (COJECO).

priorities.text: Public safety: has called for changes to New York's bail-reform laws and sanctuary-state policies, including support for legislation described as 'Laken's Law.'
Opioid crisis: advocated for the 'Fentanyl Fathers and Mothers Act' (A.8540), which would require the state to develop programs addressing the opioid crisis.

positions.summary: Called for changes to the state's sanctuary policies and the Protect Our Courts Act after a Suffolk County case in which federal agents could not take custody of undocumented individuals released without bail, saying the current policies put communities at risk.
positions.quote: Albany Majority lawmakers bail reform and sanctuary state policies are once again putting criminals ahead of victims. For years, my colleagues and I have raised concerns about these so-called reforms, yet Majority continues to ignore the warning signs.

record.text: Sponsor of a bill (A5317) requiring the safe removal of icicles from buildings abutting paved sidewalks, with civil and criminal penalties for noncompliance; referred to the Codes Committee.
Sponsor of a bill (A5336) establishing the crime of unlawful dissemination of a security body scan as a class A misdemeanor; referred to the Codes Committee.
Attended a bipartisan press conference advocating for the Fentanyl Fathers and Mothers Act (A.8540) to address the opioid crisis.
Joined a press conference calling for changes to New York's bail laws and the Protect Our Courts Act after a Suffolk County incident involving undocumented individuals released without bail.
Serves on the Assembly Aging, Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Cities, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Election Law, and Housing Committees for the 2025-2026 session.

candidates.name: Chris McCreight
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 64.2% of the vote

summary.text: Chris McCreight is the Democratic and Working Families Party candidate challenging incumbent Alec Brook-Krasny in Assembly District 46. He won a contested June 2026 Democratic primary and is a Brooklyn Democratic district leader who previously lost this seat to Brook-Krasny in 2024.

background.text: A former small-business owner who currently serves as Senior Advisor to NYC Councilmember Kayla Santosuosso; previously spent eight years as Chief of Staff to former Councilmember Justin Brannan.
Prior to his City Council work, he served as Communications and Policy Director in the New York State Assembly.
Serves as a Democratic District Leader for Bay Ridge, Dyker Heights, Coney Island, Brighton Beach, and Sea Gate.

priorities.text: "Southern Brooklyn needs a strong voice that fights for us. I'm dedicated to better public schools, a clean environment, protecting women's rights, and sensible gun laws. I'll also work to keep Bay Ridge, Coney Island, Dyker Heights, and Sea Gate safe, affordable, and welcoming for everyone."
Affordability: will fight to expand affordable healthcare, deliver universal free childcare, cut taxes for working- and middle-class families, and provide rebates for seniors on fixed incomes.

Transit and infrastructure: calls for more local control over NYC's mass transit and emergency funding for infrastructure upgrades, and wants tolls collected on NYC bridges to go to NYC transit rather than subsidize Long Island and Westchester.

Public safety: supports increasing penalties for reckless driving and ghost license plates, opposes the state's current bail-reform laws and wants judges to have more sentencing discretion, and wants to crack down on quality-of-life crimes like retail theft and illegal cannabis shops.

positions.summary: Platform calls for delivering universal free childcare for southern Brooklyn families.
Campaign says he champions gun-safety legislation and fully funding red-flag laws.
positions.quote: Champions common-sense gun safety legislation and fully funding red flag laws.

positions.summary: Supports legislation expanding access to reproductive services, empowering providers, and addressing maternal mortality.
Says he stands firmly against ICE overreach and will fight to protect immigrant communities and keep families together.
positions.quote: Chris stands firmly against ICE overreach and will fight to protect immigrant communities, keep families together, and ensure our city remains a safe haven for all.

researchNotes: Neither candidate has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Brook-Krasny's campaign website (abkforassembly.com) has an issues page that repeatedly failed to load during research, so his positions rely on his official Assembly press releases and bill sponsorships, which do not cover most of the fixed issue list; only one position (immigration_enforcement) could be documented directly, per the no-inference standard. McCreight's positions are from his campaign website; he has not held elected office, so he has no official voting or bill-sponsorship record.
